chapter: Carnegie Hall and the touring years
title: The Southern blues scene and the Houston hotel where bands stayed
summary: Blues singers like B. B. King and T-Bone Walker played; Houston's Dixon hotel housed the entertainers and booked by local promoters.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Did you hear any blues down there that you hadn't heard before?

They was, uh...playin' my records, B.B. King's records, Lowell Fulson, T-Bone Walker. They was the favorite blues singers. Charles Brown, Ray Charles--we's all...we's all hangin' out down there together. Bobby Blue Bland. We was all down South at the same time but we wasn't playin' the same towns but we run into one another down there place called...lemme see what the name of that joint was... Old Man Dixons's Place. He had a...built a brand new hotel down there.

In Houston, Texas. So we had a lotta re...we had a lotta rooms so that's where all the bands stayed. All the entertainers stayed at his place. So we play outa different towns...we go outa different towns and play overnight, and we come right back to this ...come back to the hotel every night.
Uhhh...had some promoters down there...Russo. R.J. Russo was a booker, and...uh, John Roby was a booker. Lee Morgan was a booker.
